item.title: Simplismart raises $14 Mn from Dallas Venture Capital, NVIDIA and others
item.description:
AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.

The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its inference engine and orchestration platform, expand its cloud provider network and support its growth across North America and other global markets.

Entrackr had earlier reported on the deal, which values the company at around $100 million post money. Previously, Simplismart raised $7 million in a Series A round in October 2024.

Founded by Amritanshu Jain, Simplismart provides infrastructure that helps enterprises deploy and run AI models while optimising inference costs, latency and GPU utilisation. Its platform also enables cloud providers to convert their GPU capacity into AI services for enterprise customers.

The company said its annualised revenue run rate grew 14X over the past six months. Its customers include HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema, which use its platform for production workloads across video, voice, multimodal and enterprise AI applications.

Simplismart also works with cloud providers to offer managed AI inference services. At Yotta, its platform powers the serverless inference layer of Shakti Studio, which allows customers to run AI models without managing the underlying infrastructure.

Unlike inference providers that procure or reserve GPU capacity and resell it, Simplismart focuses on the software layer that enables third party GPU infrastructure to support production AI workloads. The company is also working with cloud providers and sovereign AI programmes across India, North America, the Middle East, Australia and East Asia.

The startup plans to use the new capital to further develop its inference and orchestration capabilities and build partnerships aimed at matching AI workloads with available GPU capacity across regions and cloud environments.

item.title: Trivia and puzzle app dubdub raises seed funding led by 3one4 Capital, Antler and Stellaris
item.description:
dubdub, a swipe-based trivia and puzzle app, has raised $1.3 million in a seed funding round co-led by 3one4 Capital, Antler and Stellaris Venture Partners.

The fresh funds will be used to hire across product and engineering, add new interactive formats and deepen personalisation of its feed, dubdub said in a press release.

Launched in March this year by Kaustubh Priye and Supan Shah, dubdub is a swipe-based trivia and puzzle platform that brings bite-sized questions, mini games and brain puzzles into a short-form, interactive format.

The platform offers content across more than 20 categories, including cricket, Bollywood, general knowledge, pop culture, mythology and logical reasoning. It uses AI and user interactions to personalise challenges based on individual interests. The app also offers features that allow users to challenge friends and compare scores.

The platform aims to replace passive content consumption with questions and mini games. Each swipe prompts users to answer, guess, solve, recognise, predict or compete, making the experience more interactive.

dubdub claims to have crossed 20,000 downloads. The company also reports early retention rates above the top percentile of casual games.

It plans to expand its product and engineering teams and introduce new interactive formats as it works towards building a broader interactive short-form entertainment platform.

item.title: Ola Electric shares rally nearly 20% ahead of Q2 FY27 results
item.description:
Ola Electric Mobility shares rallied 19.5% to Rs 35.78 on Tuesday, October 27, as the electric two-wheeler maker’s Rs 1,000 crore rights issue remained in focus. 

Ola Electric’s Rs 1,000 crore rights issue opened on October 22 and closes on October 30. The company is issuing 37.03 crore partly paid-up shares at Rs 27 apiece, with an upfront payment of Rs 16.20 per share. Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors have applied for 2.39 crore shares, while founder Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake to fund his participation.

The rally comes amid SoftBank affiliate SVF II Ostrich (DE) LLC’s stake sale in Ola Electric. According to a regulatory filing, the investment vehicle sold shares and rights entitlements between January 6 and October 22, reducing its stake from 12.9% to 11.7%.

The rally follows a 14% jump in Ather Energy shares on Monday after the rival electric two-wheeler maker reported a turnaround in Q2 FY27, with a net profit of Rs 1.26 crore against a loss of Rs 154 crore in the year-ago quarter.

According to Vahan data, Ola Electric ranked fifth with 13,449 registrations and a 6.49% market share, down 3.53% from 13,941 units in August.

The company is yet to file its Q2 FY27 results. In Q1 FY27, Ola Electric’s revenue declined 45% year-on-year to Rs 455 crore from Rs 828 crore in Q1 FY26. At the same time, its losses widened 21% to Rs 336 crore. 

Ola Electric’s share price closed at over 16% higher Rs 34.8 per share, with a total market capitalization of Rs 17,395 crore ($1.83 billion)

item.title: Child-care startup Maasi raises Rs 6 Cr in pre-seed round
item.description:
Child-care startup Maasi has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Better Capital, with participation from Antler India. Angel investors in the round include Rapido founder Rishikesh SR, Shadowfax founder Vaibhav Khandelwal, Sumit Khandelwal, Siddhant Goyal and Multiply Ventures’ Sanjay Ramakrishnan.

The proceeds will be used to scale caregiver recruitment and training, build technology platforms and expand the team in Bengaluru, Maasi said in a press release.

Founded last year by Aashu Manchali, Gargi Pandey and Reshov Roy, Maasi trains, pays and supports caregivers to provide families in Bengaluru with trusted, accountable childcare at home.

The startup said its public launch on October 20 generated a waitlist of more than 4,000 parents within five days. It has served over 1,200 parents through a network of more than 500 caregivers and is growing 20% week on week.

Maasi offers on-demand nannies starting at Rs 199 per hour and monthly subscriptions starting at Rs 5,999. All caregivers undergo verification and training before meeting families through a free programme led by preschool directors, nurses and former airline cabin crew trainers.

Its latest offering, Maasi Governess, is an English-speaking nanny service focused on screen-free engagement and childcare.

item.title: IvyCap Ventures leads Rs 130 Cr pre-Series B round in Live2.ai
item.description:
Live2.ai, an AI-based social intelligence and commerce activation platform, has raised Rs 130 crore (about $14 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The round comprises primary capital for business growth and a secondary component that provides partial liquidity to early shareholders.

The fresh funds will be used to develop its agentic intelligence layer, expand its go-to-market operations for enterprise and global consumer brands, and strengthen its regional cloud infrastructure across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific, Live2.ai said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by J Venkat, Neha Suyal and Yash Arora, Live2.ai provides a platform that connects social intelligence with campaign execution and commerce activation.

The platform helps brands monitor online conversations, plan and publish social media posts, track performance, manage audits and compliance for influencer and user-generated content, and convert rights-cleared content into shoppable experiences across digital and offline channels.

The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform combines a unified entity graph, multimodal AI and autonomous AI agents. It monitors brand conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X and review sites to help brands identify trends and inform business decisions.

Live2.ai offers three key capabilities: social intelligence for trend identification and campaign strategy; audit and compliance management for influencer and user-generated content; and social publishing and performance tracking across channels.

The platform also uses eight AI agents, including Crisis Detection, Trend Scout, Campaign Auditor and Autonomous Response, to support tasks across social intelligence, campaign management and customer engagement. These agents operate on a shared entity graph with governance controls and human review.

Live2.ai said it works with brands such as Henkel's Schwarzkopf, Salonory, Titan Brands and Shiseido. The company claims to serve more than 200 brands across the US, Europe and Southeast Asia.

The startup said its revenue grew fourfold in the past 12 months, with 90% of its revenue generated outside India.
